output.title: Spot survivorship bias before it skews your sample
output.body:
When you look at only the cases that made it through, you can talk yourself into a clean answer too early. That is survivorship bias: the sample is visible, but the missing cases are not.

For a small business, this usually shows up in ordinary decisions. You review only active customers, only successful orders, or only the suppliers that are still in the mix, then assume the pattern is the whole story. The risk is not philosophical. It is rework, delayed decisions, and a lot of manual checking later.

The practical question is simple: what decision are you making from samples right now, and how would you know early that it was heading the wrong way?

A good first step is manual. Pick one recent decision made from incomplete data and write down three things: what was visible, what was missing, and what would have changed if the missing cases had been in view from the start. That gives you a real workflow boundary instead of a vague worry.

If the sample is easy to export or log, a spreadsheet check may be enough. If the cases are scattered, anecdotal, or need heavy judgment, AI may not be the right tool yet. Either way, the test comes first; the tool comes second. A tidy sample can be persuasive in the wrong direction.
